scenes.heading: Proxy Component Pattern
scenes.narration: Components. Proxy Component Pattern. In this video we review 7 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: According to best practice, what should a content resource's sling:resourceType point to?
scenes.heading: A site-specific component, not a component shared by multiple sites
scenes.body: The proxy pattern section says best practice is for sling:resourceType on content to point to a site-specific component, not one shared directly by multiple sites.
scenes.narration: According to best practice, what should a content resource's sling:resourceType point to? A site-specific component, not a component shared by multiple sites. The proxy pattern section says best practice is for sling:resourceType on content to point to a site-specific component, not one shared directly by multiple sites.

scenes.question: Why is it better for content to point to a site-specific component instead of a shared one?
scenes.heading: It lets one site customize behavior without affecting other sites
scenes.body: The speech explains that site-specific components give flexibility: if one site needs different behavior, the customization happens on its own component without affecting other sites.

scenes.question: How does a project component avoid duplicating shared component code?
scenes.heading: It points to the shared parent with sling:resourceSuperType
scenes.body: The speech says the project component refers to the shared parent with sling:resourceSuperType so code does not have to be duplicated.

scenes.question: What is a proxy component?
scenes.heading: A project component that mostly refers to a parent through sling:resourceSuperType
scenes.body: The proxy component pattern section says a project component that mostly just refers to a parent through sling:resourceSuperType is called a proxy component.

scenes.question: Can a proxy component be completely empty?
scenes.heading: Yes. It can be only a cq:Component node with a resourceSuperType when it fully inherits everything
scenes.body: The speech explicitly says a proxy can be entirely empty, only a cq:Component node with a resourceSuperType, if it fully inherits the functionality.

scenes.question: Why should you never modify Core Components code directly?
scenes.heading: Because it makes them unsupported and breaks upgrades
